STANZA I
How tedious and tasteless the hours
How tedious and tasteless the hours,
When JESUS no longer I see;
Sweet prospects, sweet birds, and sweet flow’rs,
Have lost all their sweetness with me:
The mid–summer sun shines but dim,
The fields strive in vain to look gay;
But when I am happy in Him,
December’s as pleasant as May.
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Where Newton found it
Newton printed the hymn under Psalm 73:25. The line that comes closest to it is marked.
Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You. PSALM 73:25 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 73

Content with beholding his face, My all to his pleasure resigned; No changes of season or place, Would make any change in my mind: While blessed with a sense of his love, A palace a toy would appear; And prisons would palaces prove, If JESUS would dwell with me there. STANZA III
